report.summary: These are test-hardening changes plus a Dockerfile permission fix: a gate replaces a 300 ms sleep, the R2 failure in the conversation test only hits the transcript key, and /opt/tempo and /opt/tempo/pi become traversable (0755) so the pi profile can be read. The logic is sound and the removed timing check is still covered elsewhere (ops.test.ts line 2122). I could not run typecheck because the worktree has no node_modules, and the new test uses Promise.withResolvers, an ES2024 API, while apps/tempo compiles with lib ES2023 and no repo types declare it. That would likely make `bun run typecheck` fail with TS2550. Running typecheck at this commit is needed before merge.

findings.text: Promise.withResolvers is ES2024, but apps/tempo/tsconfig.json and tsconfig.base.json use lib ES2023, and nothing in the repo (worker-runtime.d.ts included) declares PromiseConstructor.withResolvers. apps/tempo's typecheck includes the test folder, so this most likely fails with TS2550 and breaks `bun run typecheck` (CLAUDE.md rule 15). Not confirmed because node_modules is missing; running `bun run typecheck` would confirm it. Fix: use a hand-made resolver (`let release!: () => void; const gate = new Promise<void>((r) => (release = r));`) or raise the lib setting.

evidence.why: The compile setting is "lib": ["ES2023", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"], and withResolvers only exists in lib.es2024.promise.

checked.risk: Tests: sleeps/timing assertions replaced with observable waits, gate always released, no zero-assertion paths, timing coverage kept
Tests: shared spy on env.DATA.put under a shared test file now only fails the conversation key; key matches the production key
Build/runtime environment: file modes for /opt/tempo/pi/tempo-profile.ts readable by the tempo user, interaction with the test image and the spec path
Build: typecheck of changed test files against the configured lib (could not run tsc; no node_modules)
Spec / security / contracts / idempotency: no production code, spec, secrets or platform calls changed
